REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - DECEMBER 14, 2023 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, DECEMBER 14,
2023, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

 1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

 2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

 3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council/Agency Member Chuong Vo.

 4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Chuong Vo
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Bruce W. Barrows

 5.  Presentations/Appointments

 5A.  Presentations

  A plaque and certificate were presented by the City Council honoring:

  Alan Strickland (Twenty-five years of service to the City of Cerritos).

 5B.  Review and consideration of selection of a voting delegate and alternate to represent the
  City of Cerritos on the Independent Cities Association Board of Directors (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Cynthia Nava, City Clerk Division Manager.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period
  closed.

  MOTION: There was unanimous City Council action to designate Councilmember Johnson as
  the voting delegate and Councilmember Yokoyama as the voting alternate to represent the
  City on the Independent Cities Association (ICA) Board of Directors. As a result of this
  action, the City Clerk will notify the ICA of the City’s designation of the voting delegate and
  alternate and add this item to the list of Mayor’s Annual Appointments for City Council
  consideration each year that the City remains a member of the organization (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, December 14, 2023, 7:00 p.m.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  In-Person Public Comments:

  M. Villa requested the City Council take action to support H.Res. 786 - Calling for an
  immediate de-escalation and cease-fire in Israel and occupied Palestine.

  Ernie Nishii thanked the City Council for their service and offered his assistance as a
  resource in his capacity as the ABC Unified School District Board’s liaison to the City of
  Cerritos.

  Teddy Lloyd commented on the Parks and Recreation Commission’s recent review of the
  feasibility of additional pickleball courts in the City. He requested that the City Council
  expedite their review of any resulting recommendations.

  Juan Martinez requested that the City Council take action in support of H.Res. 786 - Calling
  for an immediate de-escalation and cease-fire in Israel and occupied Palestine.

  Yuri Preciado requested the City Council take action in support of H.Res. 786 - Calling for
  an immediate de-escalation and cease-fire in Israel and occupied Palestine.

  (Written correspondence submitted by the deadline listed on the agenda is considered

  text, unredacted written correspondence that was submitted for this item. Public requests
  for copies of the written correspondence submitted for this meeting can be made during
  regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer.)

  Jonathan Hawes requested the City Council adopt a resolution opposing alleged actions
  taken by certain elected and appointed officials in the City of El Monte.

  Malik Tariq Mahmood Murabbi Silsilah expressed his personal faith beliefs.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7B.2. Approval of Fiscal Year 2023-24 Budget Amendments (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Johnson, to authorize administrative-
  initiated Fiscal Year 2023-24 budget amendments in accordance with Joint Budget Resolution
  No. 2023-26 / No. CSA 2023-01 and the Strategic Financial Plan and Budget Preparation
  Policy (Policy 2.04) as adopted by the City Council, as follows:

  1. Account/Project: cp17199 Groundwater Remediation-Civic Center
  Amount: $450,329
  Justification: Various change orders were issued to the contractor, some of which
  included integrating new pumps into the SCADA system, relocating existing utilities,
  installing extra electrical equipment, removing and installing concrete in the drive aisle
  and adjustment for quantities. A change order is also needed for additional construction
  management, which covers structural design and special inspections.

  2. Account/Project: cp12706 CCPA Roof Replacement
  Amount: $215,360
  Justification: Two (2) change orders involved essential modifications to the project.
  Under Change Order No. 1, the contractor was requested to replace caulking at tile
  joints above the barrel roof due to natural wear, apply a suitable joint sealant for
  Polyurethane bonding, and extend waterproofing wall limits to cover existing cracks.
  Change Order No. 2 involved addressing leakage in the mechanical room, which
  necessitated preparation and installation of deck and wall coating in the mechanical
  room at the Sierra Room. These changes were made to ensure the integrity and
  functionality of the project's infrastructure (COUNCIL).
